prompt:
I need the front end for Stockroom. An in-house asset library run by the creative services department of a national home-goods retailer, holding every approved product photo, lifestyle shoot, and packaging file the brand is allowed to use.

Who's using it: Priya Raman, a senior packaging designer on the 40-person in-house creative team. She knows the brand guidelines well but rarely deals with photo licensing, which the department's rights coordinator manages.

What they're doing right now: She is laying out the front panel of a holiday gift-set box for the 'Ember' stoneware line and needs one hero lifestyle photo showing the 4-piece mug set on a table setting. It has to be landscape, at least 6000 px wide, cleared for print packaging, and licensed through at least next December. She has already turned down two shots because the model release only covers digital use. Now she is narrowing the remaining candidates to a handful she can show her art director this afternoon, then choosing one to request a high-res download for.

What's in the system at this point: 14,280 assets total. 312 are tagged 'Ember stoneware' across 9 shoots (2023–2026), including 'Ember Fall Table – Studio 4, Aug 2026' (86 images) and 'Ember Cabin Lifestyle – Asheville, Oct 2025' (54 images). Each asset has photographer, shoot date, orientation, pixel dimensions, color profile, products pictured (SKU numbers such as EMB-MUG4-SLT), usage rights (web, social, print-ad, packaging, in-store), license expiry date (e.g. 2027-03-31), model/property release status, approval state (approved, pending retouch, retired), and download count. 23 Ember images are marked retired and 11 are still pending retouch. Priya has 6 assets saved to a personal 'Holiday box' collection.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
